public_rationale: Epoch's earlier work provides a substantive basis for concern about an approaching shortage of high-quality text. It does not establish that LLMs broadly were running out during the target period. The June update changed the estimated timing and methodology, but concerns a later period. The evidence supports the plausibility of a data constraint without settling the claim's breadth and timing.
limitations: A credible forecast of a future bottleneck is not proof that the bottleneck already existed.
The result could change under a narrower reading limited to particular high-quality corpora.
The legal-consequences forecast is outside this claim's normalized scope.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs are running out of training data.

statement.excerpt: As I wrote (and broadcast) recently, LLMs are running out of training data, and the desperation to find more will lead to significant legal consequences when it's revealed exactly how much they stole and from whom they stole it from.

from_speaker: LLMs are running out of training data
our_interpretation: This assessment covers the supplied normalized proposition about data availability. It does not grade the separate forecast of legal consequences in the same sentence.

The ordinary reading is that frontier LLM training was approaching a shortage of useful additional human-generated text at prevailing scaling rates, rather than that every possible training source was already exhausted.
A projection can inform that assessment, but its assumptions and distinction between high-quality text and all usable data must be preserved.
No period is stated. I use 2024 through publication as the current-state reporting window.
criteria.support_condition: Stock-and-demand estimates applicable to the target period show useful additional training text approaching exhaustion at prevailing frontier training rates.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable estimates applicable to the target period show that usable new data was not approaching a constraint under then-current training practices.

evidence.excerpt: the model uncertainty is very high.
evidence.explanation: The study projected high-quality language-data exhaustion before 2026, while projecting much later limits for lower-quality language data. It explicitly qualified those projections and did not measure an April 2024 shortage.

The later update projected a future constraint and revised the earlier high-quality-data estimate. Its changed methodology cautions against treating the earlier projection as an established current shortage.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An estimate or retrospective reconstruction specifically covering early 2024, comparing usable remaining text with frontier training demand and stating the quality, access, and repetition assumptions.
